pages.title: Permanent Links
pages.text: A book is a door you carry. A $(thing)Crystal Portal$() is a door that agrees to stay put. $(br)$(br)Build a closed frame of $(c)Crystal Blocks$(). It may stand upright or lie flat, and it need not be a perfect rectangle, but the crystal must complete its ring.

pages.title: Ignition
pages.text: One stone of the frame must be a $(c)Book Receptacle$(), touching at least one Crystal. When the frame is sealed, place a linked Linking Book or Descriptive Book within it. The passage wakes at once with a random retained hue. Linking Books preserve their exact position and facing; Descriptive Books lead to the Age's safe arrival anchor.

Take away the book, or break the crystal ring, and the road collapses without ceremony. I have seen pursuers vanish mid-step this way. I have also seen friends do the same, so be certain before meddling.

pages.title: Portal Controls
pages.text: While a receptacle holds a book, use a $(item)Crystal Block$() on it to rotate the destination facing 90 degrees clockwise. With Immersive Portals installed, use $(item)Shears$() to hide or restore Mystcraft's colored surface while leaving the seamless portal active. Either control preserves the book.

pages.title: Bottling Ink
pages.text: A glass bottle and an ink sac make an $(thing)Ink Vial$(). It is useful at the writing desk, but builders have discovered another purpose.

pages.title: Painting Crystal
pages.text: Craft one $(thing)Ink Vial$() with one model-rendered block that has no block entity. The sampled block is consumed and yields a vial with $(thing)16 uses$(); Crystal and portal components cannot be sampled. Use it on a Crystal face to cover only that face. Different faces may carry different patterns. The empty vial returns when exhausted.

pages.title: Recovering the Frame
pages.text: Crystal Blocks and the Book Receptacle share the same mining requirements. Bring an $(thing)iron pickaxe$() or better if you wish to recover either one intact.
